unit_goal_source: Observed defect, standalone unit: docs/backlog/distribution/isolate-host-unhandled-rejection-lost-to-gc.md (Context + `## Decisions` 2026-11-19 user line: declared ceiling, no product change, upstream https://github.com/laverdet/isolated-vm/issues/589); baseline = live `node -e` v24.16.0 exit 1 + diagnostic. BASE 9b948d757 (origin main, merge of PR #412), HEAD 4f0c57c43.

coverage.row: The defect is pinned as a declared ceiling in both lanes (runCode and the README embedder): the rows stay literal against live `node -e` and run as expected failures, so a fixed isolated-vm turns them red
The documented consumer workaround (handle every promise; `.catch` that sets `process.exitCode`) gives Node's result under the same GC pressure in both lanes

findings.evidence: runCode("queueMicrotask(() => process.exit(2))", {timeoutMs:3000}) -> exitCode null, termination 'timeout', stderr 'Error: process exit requires an active control port\n    at #requestSelfExit (rifty-isolate-guest.js:105159:15) ...'; node -e -> 2, stderr ''
findings.summary: The new `process.exit()` from a microtask row says 'output kept' but not that stderr also gains a rifty-internal 'process exit requires an active control port' stack; a consumer reading stderr sees internal frames. Worth one clause in the row or the backlog item.

findings.evidence: rows.mjs x5: main().then(() => process.exit(0)) node 0 / runCode null+timeout 5/5; process.on('exit', () => { Promise.reject(new Error('r')) }) node 1+stderr / runCode 0, stderr '' 5/5
findings.summary: Two discoveries ride the branch as compat rows + backlog drafts (PR-1 allows it; both measured correctly), but neither has a ceiling corpus row, so a later fix leaves those compat rows stale with nothing turning red. Hardening for isolate-host-queuemicrotask-throw-times-out / isolate-host-rejection-in-exit-listener-exits-0, not required by this unit.

findings.evidence: Pre-existing mechanism, not changed by the diff. Stock run: the four ceiling rows fail on exitCode 0 vs node's 1 with stderr '' (rows.mjs 5/5 each), so they fail for the declared reason today.
findings.summary: `it.fails` accepts any failure, so a ceiling row would stay green if the run later failed differently (e.g. timeout, crash). Pinning the observed wrong outcome (`exitCode: 0, stderr: ''`) would make the ceiling discriminate its own failure mode; advisory.
